paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Habakkuk brings his hardest question straight to the LORD, and he starts by remembering who he's talking to: "Are You not from everlasting, O LORD, my God, my Holy One?" (Habakkuk 1:12). Then he lets the whole thing out, the silence, the unfairness, all of it (Habakkuk 1:13). The LORD never scolds him for asking, and that tells me a baker can bring the real question and not the polite one.

Now look at what Habakkuk does next. He says, "I will stand at my guard post and station myself on the ramparts. I will watch to see what He will say to me…" (Habakkuk 2:1). He asks, and then he stays to listen. I think that's the hard part, because I have asked a question and walked off before the answer showed up, and I looked like a stamper who left the oven door open and went to find his hat. The LORD answers him, and He says the vision "awaits an appointed time" and "will surely come and will not delay" (Habakkuk 2:3).

So how do we live while we wait? The LORD gives the answer in one short line: "the righteous will live by faith" (Habakkuk 2:4). Next to that sits the proud one, whose soul is not upright and who is never satisfied (Habakkuk 2:4-5). Faith means trusting the LORD while the oven is still warming and the answer isn't out yet, and that's what Habakkuk is being shown. The teaching isn't over, either, so keep your apron on.
